audit_notes: Parameters are positive and within their bounds. Derived streamwise slip length for lubricant-filled longitudinal grooves: pitch L = w/(1-phi_s) = 28.6 um; shear-free-groove slip (Philip/Lauga-Stone) b_gas = (L/pi) ln(sec(pi(1-phi_s)/2)) = 7.18 um; correction for a viscous infill with viscosity ratio N = 0.463 and aspect w/d = 1.33 gives b = 7.18/1.617 = 4.44 um. With a viscous-sublayer Couette gap H = 25 um this gives b/H = 0.178 and a wall-shear reduction b/(H+b) ~ 15 % at fixed sublayer-edge velocity. This laminar Couette picture overstates the turbulent benefit: in wall units b+ = b u_tau/nu ~ 0.93 (u_tau = sqrt(50/1025) = 0.22 m/s), for which turbulent-channel DNS and the Fukagata-Kasagi-Koumoutsakos relation give only ~4-6 % skin-friction reduction at ship Reynolds numbers; the simulated gain must be read as an upper bound. Capillary retention: Laplace pressure ~ 2*0.025/2e-5 = 2.5 kPa vs turbulent wall-pressure fluctuations p_rms ~ 2-3 tau_w ~ 100-150 Pa, so pinning is plausible, but shear-driven drainage along the grooves (flux per groove ~ tau*w*d^2/(3 mu_o) order 1e-9 m3/s over long grooves) requires segmentation of the grooves into closed cells or continuous replenishment; the porous feed must be sized for this. Material/structural check: ridges 8.6 um wide and 15 um tall in a hard polymer (E ~ 2-3 GPa) see only ~50 Pa shear: no collapse; abrasion (fenders, cleaning brushes) is the real durability threat. Environmental: the lubricant is discharged into the sea at the replenishment rate; it must be non-toxic and biodegradable (e.g. light hydrocarbons or short silicones), which is a regulatory risk but not a physics failure. Baseline: the same wall without grooves (groove_width = 0 makes the slip length exactly zero), i.e. a smooth clean untreated hull in the same Couette model.

hard_constraints: relative error between solver and analytical reference below 1 %
lubricant viscosity below water viscosity (otherwise no net slip)
Laplace pressure of the groove meniscus at least 10x the turbulent wall-pressure fluctuation

baseline_description: smooth, clean, ungrooved hull wall (no slip) in the same sublayer Couette model
